_comment: The named non-step buckets. This view is the sole owner of the af.overhead-marked events the per-step view excludes.
name: spend-outside-steps
title: Spend outside steps
description: Every request that no step owns, grouped by why. Quality-gate and fidelity-gate work appears as grader-overhead; spend before a run's first step began appears as unattributed; a session with no formula running appears as no-formula. Naming these rather than discarding them is what lets the reconciliation check add up.
af_decision_o4: O-4 (view delivery) is hybrid: files on disk plus a best-effort dashboard push. See README.md.
af_assumptions: COLUMN SPELLINGS AND JOIN VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE BACKEND, THIS QUERY NOT EXECUTED: during review of PR #567 OpenObserve v0.91.3 was stood up from the pinned artifact and the per-step token view's query was run verbatim, confirming the ingest naming this view also relies on. This view's own query was NOT among those executed. This view computes max(af_step_seq) inside its step_windows CTE but never orders on it or emits it, so it is deliberately left uncast. A dashboard already published under this title is never replaced by a re-run of quickstart.sh, so an existing factory keeps the query it first received — re-import this file by hand to pick up changes. CI has no backend, so none of this is re-verified automatically.

The native claude_code.api_request shape (input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd) is the synthetic fixture's hypothesis, not a recorded capture - see internal/telemetry/testdata/synthetic/api_request_events.json, which P6b replaces. Whether these arrive as OTel logs or metrics is also an inference; if it is metrics, the stream name and column prefix both change.

Attribute names are rewritten on ingest. Trace resource attributes are prefixed with 'service_' and every dot becomes an underscore, so af.formula_instance is queryable only as service_af_formula_instance. OTLP logs do NOT get the prefix, so the same attribute is af_formula_instance on the native-event side of the join. _timestamp is microseconds while start_time/end_time are nanoseconds and duration is microseconds.

session-start, inter-step and compaction are named as buckets but are not separately derivable from the event shape recorded so far; they currently fall under unattributed. Splitting them needs richer native attributes and is P6b work.

dashboard.title: Spend outside steps
dashboard.description: Every request no step owns, grouped by why.

queries.query:
WITH step_windows AS (
    -- Rule 2, earliest start wins. The af side has already applied earliest-wins when it computed
    -- each step's duration, and only closed steps are exported, so in practice this aggregates one
    -- row per step. MIN/MAX are kept because the rule must survive a second span for the same step
    -- arriving later - a wide window is visible in the reconciliation view, a narrow one is not.
    SELECT service_af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
           af_step_id                  AS step,
           service_af_agent            AS agent,
           max(af_step_seq)            AS step_order,
           max(af_model)               AS model,
           min(start_time)             AS window_start_ns,
           max(end_time)               AS window_end_ns
    FROM "traces"."default"
    WHERE service_name = 'agentfactory'
      AND af_step_id <> ''
    GROUP BY service_af_formula_instance, af_step_id, service_af_agent
),
requests AS (
    SELECT af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
           af_agent            AS agent,
           af_overhead,
           _timestamp * 1000   AS at_ns,
           input_tokens,
           output_tokens,
           cost_usd
    FROM "logs"."default"
),
classified AS (
    SELECT r.*,
           CASE
               -- This view OWNS the overhead-marked events: it is the sole owner, which is what
               -- lets the per-step view exclude them without the spend disappearing. The suffix
               -- matches what AttributeEvent produces, so a grader event lands in
               -- 'grader-overhead' on both sides. The bucket name IS the contract. An empty marker
               -- is not a marker, matching AttributeEvent.
               WHEN r.af_overhead IS NOT NULL AND r.af_overhead <> ''
                   THEN r.af_overhead || '-overhead'
               -- Spend by a session with no formula running at all.
               WHEN r.formula_run IS NULL OR r.formula_run = '' THEN 'no-formula'
               -- Spend before this agent's first step of the run began: session startup, or a
               -- formula that never got going. The agent predicate matches the one the per-step
               -- view joins on; without it an event from an agent that never closed a step would
               -- be classed as step-attributed here and join nothing there, vanishing from both.
               WHEN NOT EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1 FROM step_windows w
                   WHERE w.formula_run = r.formula_run
                     AND w.agent       = r.agent
                     AND r.at_ns >= w.window_start_ns
               ) THEN 'unattributed'
               ELSE 'step-attributed'
           END AS bucket
    FROM requests r
)
SELECT bucket,
       formula_run,
       agent,
       count(*)                          AS requests,
       sum(input_tokens)                 AS input_tokens,
       sum(output_tokens)                AS output_tokens,
       sum(input_tokens + output_tokens) AS total_tokens,
       sum(cost_usd)                     AS cost_usd_reported
FROM classified
-- Rows the per-step view already owns are not repeated here. The two views use the same
-- instance-and-agent scoping, so between them every request has exactly one owner.
WHERE bucket <> 'step-attributed'
GROUP BY bucket, formula_run, agent
ORDER BY total_tokens DESC
